findings.title: canManage() treats VIEW-only group permission as sufficient to manage groups
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg, realm-wide check), the method returns true via `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` — i.e. it accepts either VIEW or MANAGE scope. This is identical to canView()'s body except for the admin-role check, and it means an admin who was granted only a read-only 'view' permission on the Groups resource type is treated as if they also have 'manage' permission. Since GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls `auth.groups().requireManage()` to authorize creating new top-level groups, a user with only VIEW scope on Groups would be able to create (and, via other requireManage() call sites, modify) groups, which is a privilege escalation. Compare with canManage(GroupModel) and canManageMembership(GroupModel) in the same class, and with UserPermissions.canManage(), none of which accept VIEW as sufficient for MANAGE — confirming this is inconsistent/incorrect. The call should check only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs, and per-group resources are not discoverable
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() calls `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> ...)` to enumerate group-scoped authorization resources, then calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result set. However: (1) individual per-group resources are created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(), which never calls resource.setType(...) (unlike the legacy V1 GroupPermissions.initialize(), which explicitly sets `groupResource.setType("Group")`), so findByType(server, "Groups", ...) will not find per-group resources at all — it will only match the single 'all-groups' placeholder resource created during schema init (which does have its type set). (2) Even for that placeholder, `groupResource.getId()` is the authorization resource's own internal ID, not a GroupModel id; hasPermission(String groupId, ...) expects a real GroupModel id (it looks the resource up via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, and resources are named by the group's id per resolveGroup()). As a result this method either returns an empty set (making the group-based DB pre-filter in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource a no-op, relying solely on slower per-user canView checks) or, when an 'all-groups' VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission exists, returns a bogus id that does not correspond to any real group, which would be used as a UserModel.GROUPS search filter and could incorrectly exclude all users even though the admin should see them via blanket group-membership permission. This should use `groupResource.getName()` (not getId()) and the underlying resources need a type set so findByType can actually locate them.

findings.title: getResourceName() does not resolve a friendly display name for Group resources
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to translate the resource's internal name (the user's UUID) into the user's username (or 'All users' for the catch-all resource), but no equivalent branch was added for the newly introduced GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE even though group resources are created the same way (named by the group's UUID via resolveGroup()). As a consequence, any UI or API that calls getResourceName() for a group-scoped scope-permission will fall through to `resource.getDisplayName()` and show the raw group UUID (or whatever default display name is stored) instead of the group's actual name, unlike the symmetric behavior implemented for Users.

findings.title: Removed short-circuit for global group-view permission when listing subgroups
findings.body: getSubGroups() previously computed `canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView()` once and used `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g))`, short-circuiting per-subgroup evaluation when the caller already has global view rights. The change replaces this with `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)`, which invokes canView(GroupModel) for every subgroup even when the admin already has global view permission. For FGAP V2, canView(GroupModel) performs a resource lookup and policy evaluation per call, so for groups with many subgroups this reintroduces an evaluation (and potential DB query) per subgroup instead of a single check, which is a performance regression compared to the previous behavior.

findings.title: Removed short-circuit for global group-view permission when listing top-level groups
findings.body: getGroups() previously cached `canViewGlobal = groupsEvaluator.canView()` and used `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || groupsEvaluator.canView(g))` to avoid a per-group permission evaluation when the caller already has blanket view rights. This was changed to `.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`, so canView(GroupModel) — which for FGAP V2 can trigger a resource lookup and policy evaluation — now runs once per group returned by the query instead of being short-circuited by a single global check, which can be a notable performance regression for realms with many groups.

findings.title: Admin fine-grained authz event listener registration now gated at registration time instead of per-event
findings.body: registerListener() used to always register the ProviderEventListener and check `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` inside onEvent() for every incoming event. The change moves the feature check outside, so the listener is only registered if the feature is enabled at the moment registerListener() is invoked (typically once, at provider/session-factory initialization). If the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is toggled on after this registration happens (e.g. in test harnesses or deployments that enable the feature dynamically after providers have already been initialized), RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup of permissions will silently stop firing, whereas previously it would have resumed working as soon as the flag became true. This is a behavior change that is not obviously covered by tests.

findings.title: No negative test that VIEW-only group permission cannot be used to manage groups
findings.body: testManageAllGroups() only verifies that granting MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource allows group creation/update; there is no test asserting that an admin granted only VIEW (or VIEW_MEMBERS) scope on Groups is still forbidden from creating/updating/deleting groups. Such a test would have caught the canManage() bug in GroupPermissionsV2 where VIEW scope is incorrectly treated as sufficient for manage operations. Additionally, there is no test exercising an 'all-groups' level VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission and verifying that user search via group membership actually returns the expected users, which would have revealed the getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() id-mapping bug.

findings.title: Public utility method removed without deprecation
findings.body: The public static method `ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(session, realm, attributes, first, max)` was removed outright (callers were updated to call `session.groups().searchGroupsByAttributes(...)` directly in GroupsResource). Although this class lives in server-spi-private, it is a public API surface; removing a public method without a deprecation cycle can break any other internal or external module that still references it directly, since there is no compiler-visible deprecation warning period.
